scope: Read-only source review of whole_suite.py and guard.py integration with plan.md and previously tested helper interface. No whole certificate read or replayed; no root sources edited.

resolved_findings.resolution: Each constructed certificate and canonical output sidecar has a unique certificate-<case> basename. At most one full mutation remains live; sidecar hashes and paths persist in its recipe. Existing failed mutations remain untouched.

checked: Requires complete successful same-generation producer and fresh verifier receipts before reading the proof.
Rehashes exact production binary, frozen preparation/profile, input copies and original proof; verifies same certificate and complete semantic report fields.
Two controls include explicitly reused original actual fresh verification and required byte-identical rechain with new production verification.
Matrix enumerates ten context/semantic binding attacks plus eight semantic and five framing cases (23 expected rejects).
Every negative requires exit 1, empty stdout, specific expected error substring, unchanged protected output.
One nonblocking global filesystem lock covers both generations and entire execution.
Guard assigns owned process group, timeout/RSS/disk sampled limits, hard CPU/file limits; terminates only owned process group.
Unexpected construction or verification failure leaves the full mutation and logs intact. Cleanup occurs only after successful classified verification and receipt save.
Corrected unique sidecar names cannot collide across payload/topology/rebound cases or with protected verifier destinations.
Read-only AST parsing confirms five alternate bindings and thirteen additional mutations: 2 controls, 10 binding rejects, 8 semantic rejects, 5 framing rejects.
limitations: Source review only; successful whole-proof eligibility and complete 23-case runtime results remain unobserved.
